signatures.title: Blue screens
signatures.what: Windows crashed with a blue screen and restarted.
signatures.impact: Unsaved work is lost each time. Repeated blue screens usually mean a faulty driver, failing memory or damaged system files.

signatures.title: Unexpected shutdowns
signatures.what: The PC went off without shutting down properly: power loss, a held power button, a flat battery or a freeze.
signatures.impact: Open work is lost and files can be damaged. If nobody caused it, it points at power, overheating or a crash.

signatures.title: A drive predicts its own failure
signatures.what: A drive's built-in health monitoring reports that it is likely to fail.
signatures.impact: Back up now. The drive can stop working without further warning, taking its files with it.

signatures.title: Drive read and write errors
signatures.what: Windows hit bad areas, or could not read the page file, on a drive.
signatures.impact: Files can be lost or damaged and the PC may freeze. Often the first sign of a failing drive.

signatures.title: A drive keeps stalling
signatures.what: Disk requests had to be retried, or the drive controller was reset.
signatures.impact: Causes freezes of several seconds. The cause is usually a failing drive, a loose cable or a storage driver.

signatures.title: File system damage
signatures.what: Windows found damage in the file system on a drive.
signatures.impact: Files or folders can become unreadable. Windows can usually repair it with a disk check at the next restart.

signatures.title: Serious hardware errors
signatures.what: The processor, memory or a device reported an error Windows could not correct.
signatures.impact: These cause blue screens and sudden restarts. Overheating, failing memory or a faulty device are the usual causes.

signatures.title: Hardware errors Windows corrected
signatures.what: The processor, memory or a PCIe device reported errors that Windows corrected.
signatures.impact: Harmless now and then. Many in a row point at overheating, memory or a loose drive or card, and can turn into crashes.

signatures.title: Graphics driver crashes
signatures.what: The graphics driver stopped responding and Windows restarted it (the screen goes black for a moment).
signatures.impact: Flicker, black screens, and crashing games or video calls. Usually fixed by updating the graphics driver.

signatures.title: {name} keeps crashing
signatures.what: {name} closed unexpectedly.
signatures.impact: Work in that app is lost each time. Repeated crashes usually need an update, a repair or a reinstall of the app.

signatures.title: {name} keeps freezing
signatures.what: {name} stopped responding and was closed.
signatures.impact: Unsaved work in that app is lost. Often an add-in, an old version, or the PC running out of memory.

signatures.title: The {name} service keeps crashing
signatures.what: The Windows service "{name}" stopped unexpectedly.
signatures.impact: Whatever relies on it (printing, sound, sign-in, sync) stops working until it restarts.

signatures.title: Windows updates are failing
signatures.what: Windows Update could not install one or more updates.
signatures.impact: The PC misses security fixes and keeps retrying in the background, which slows it down.

signatures.title: Website names keep failing to look up
signatures.what: The DNS server didn't answer when Windows looked up a name.
signatures.impact: Pages and apps fail to load at random although the connection is up.

signatures.title: The clock can't sync
signatures.what: Windows could not set the clock from a time server.
signatures.impact: A wrong clock breaks secure websites, sign-ins, Teams and Outlook.

signatures.title: Restore points were deleted
signatures.what: Windows deleted restore points (shadow copies) because space ran out.
signatures.impact: Fewer ways back if an update or a new program breaks something.

signatures.title: Restore points can't be created
signatures.what: System Restore tried to create a restore point and failed.
signatures.impact: There is no way back if an update, a driver or a new program breaks something, and DeskMedic can't make one before its riskier fixes.

signatures.title: Ran out of memory
signatures.what: Windows ran low on memory and warned that programs might close.
signatures.impact: Everything slows down and apps can close without saving.

signatures.title: Company settings aren't applying
signatures.what: Group Policy could not be processed, usually because the company network or a server wasn't reachable.
signatures.impact: Drive mappings, printers and security settings from IT may be missing or out of date.

signatures.title: The processor is being slowed down
signatures.what: The firmware limited the processor's speed, usually because of heat or the power supply.
signatures.impact: Everything feels slow. Often dust, a blocked vent, or a charger that's too weak.

signatures.title: Microsoft Defender found threats
signatures.what: Microsoft Defender detected malware or a potentially unwanted app.
signatures.impact: Usually blocked or removed already. Worth a full scan and a look at where it came from.

signatures.title: A threat could not be removed
signatures.what: Microsoft Defender found a threat but failed to remove it.
signatures.impact: Malware may still be active on this PC. Disconnect from the network and ask IT.

harmless.why: DCOM permission messages logged on almost every PC; Microsoft says to ignore them.
The same unexpected shutdown, already counted from Kernel-Power.
A secure connection to a website or service was refused, or its certificate didn't match; normal.
Licence checks that are retried later.
Logs from Windows' own small databases, usually harmless.
An old app or script asked Windows for something it no longer has.
A driver for an unplugged device didn't load at startup.
